← Audio Tools

Glitch Voice

I built Glitch Voice to bring the breath, friction, and irregular rhythms of a voice forward during live performance. The system transforms microphone input in real time, and a pressure-sensitive controller lets the performer shape the resulting vocal texture by changing their grip.

Training on two kinds of vocal gesture

I organized my experimental vocal recordings into Flow, for sustained sounds, and Burst, for short, abrupt gestures. I trained models using IRCAM’s RAVE architecture and compared checkpoints by listening to the textures they produced.

Making the models playable

I integrated the neural processing into Max/MSP and mapped grip pressure to a transition between Flow and Burst. The performer can change the balance as they speak or vocalize, using the same gesture to move gradually between sustained and more abrupt textures.

Presented at Co-Creativity in Music, Sound, and AI at UC Riverside in June 2026.
